resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register's 1900 first post and the 1957 newspaper's 1902 build date fit together: the site was first established in 1900 and the first structure built in 1902.

notes_for_editor: Many dates conflict and are reported as such in the story: current steel tower 1955-57 work, 1958 (Kamstra, Idaho Fire Lookouts) and 1959 (register); lightning death 1931 (register, newspaper) vs 1932 (Idaho Fire Lookouts); fall death 1964 (newspaper, association report) vs 1966 (register); elevation 5,477 ft (register) vs 5,520 ft (other pages). Record height_m 12.2 (40 ft) matches the 1933 pole tower, not the current 54-56 ft steel tower; left unchanged for a human decision. Record design L-4 describes the 1933 tower; current cab is 14 by 14 feet per the register. Access is set to restricted because the tower is owned by a timber association, used for emergency detection, and a 1958 report limits visitors to the observatory platform; no current rules were found. Idaho Fire Lookouts lists a 1918 tower and a 1923 glass-cabin tower as separate; sources do not settle the sequence. Staff names on Idaho Fire Lookouts were not reproduced. Checked 2026-10-08: the story no longer credits Mable Gray with the first watch on the strength of Idaho Fire Lookouts, which gives only the 1902 perch detail; Kamstra calls her the first lookout here. A 1955 association report (Forest Lookouts) dates the L-4 tower to 1934, against 1933 elsewhere; the story notes this. Only the association report calls the 1964 death accidental.
